title: Exact Entanglement Swapping through Single-Occupancy Measurements in Gaussian Fermion States
abstract: We determine the exact entanglement structure of the conditional state obtained by measuring $m$ corresponding rungs ($m\leq N/2$) in two identical copies of an arbitrary half-filled free fermion Gaussian state and post-selecting the same normalized single-fermion state ($|ψ\rangle = u|10\rangle+v|01\rangle$, where 0 and 1 denote the fermion occupancy on each sites) on each rung. For $m<N/2$, the conditional wavefunction generally depends on the initial state. Nevertheless, whenever the selected outcome has nonzero probability, the state on the unmeasured sites remains Gaussian and factorizes exactly into $N-m$ different orthogonal modes including $m$ inter-copy entangling modes and $N-2m$ spectator modes localized in one copy. Consequently, the entanglement entropy between the unmeasured parts of the two copies is $S=m h_2(|v|^2)$, independent of the initial state, where $h_2(x)=-x\ln x-(1-x)\ln(1-x)$. The success probability is given by $P_m=\det C_L\det(I_m-C_L)=\det(C_{LR}C_{RL})$, determined solely by the initial correlations and independent of ($u$,$v$). Equal-weight Bell post-selection serves as a special case that achieves the maximal entanglement swapping.
summary: This work analyzes entanglement swapping in two copies of a free fermion Gaussian state by performing single-occupancy measurements on multiple rungs. It proves that the resulting entanglement entropy in the unmeasured parts is universal, depending only on the measurement parameters. The methodology involves advanced fermionic field theory techniques to isolate the residual entangled modes.
main_problem: The paper determines the exact entanglement structure of the conditional state resulting from measuring specific rungs in two identical copies of a free fermion Gaussian state.
main_result: The entanglement entropy between the unmeasured parts of the two copies is found to be $S = m h_2(|v|^2)$, which is universal and independent of the initial state.
method: The analysis uses projection operators and canonical transformations on the fermionic state to separate the unmeasured system into residual and spectator modes.
model_or_system: The system consists of two identical copies of a half-filled free fermion Gaussian state, analyzed by post-selecting a specific single-occupancy state on $m$ measured rungs.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy ($S$), Success Probability ($P_m$), and the conditional state $|\Psi(u,v)_{	ext{post}}angle$.
important_parameters: Number of measured rungs ($m$), the single-occupancy state parameters ($u, v$), and the initial correlation structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the success probability $P_m$ is non-zero, and relies on constructing an adapted occupied-orbital basis via Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the process: initial copies, single-occupancy post-selection on rungs, and the resulting conditional state structure.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mathematical framework by adapting the occupied-orbital basis (Appendix A), calculating the success probability using determinants (Appendix B), and analyzing the residual entanglement entropy (Appendix C).
why_interesting: The result shows that entanglement swapping in this fermionic setting yields a universal entropy formula, providing a clean, analytically tractable model for entanglement manipulation beyond simple qubit systems.
